site.title: Weekly Research Digest
site.tagline: New research on entrepreneurship, generative AI and work, and organizations and inequality
site.owner_role: Assistant Professor, Tepper School of Business, Carnegie Mellon University

sets.label: Entrepreneurship
sets.description: New venture creation and growth, founders and founding teams, self-employment and small business, startup financing (venture capital, angels, accelerators, crowdfunding), firm entry and exit, entrepreneurial ecosystems and policy, who becomes an entrepreneur, and innovation and society: who becomes an inventor or innovator, the direction of innovation and whose needs it serves, social and institutional determinants of invention, and science-based and university ventures.

sets.label: Generative AI & Work
sets.description: How generative AI, large language models, and foundation models change work, tasks, occupations, labor markets, hiring, skills, productivity, creativity, management, and new venture creation.

sets.label: Organizations & Inequality
sets.description: Class and socioeconomic origins, stratification and social mobility, careers and promotion inside organizations, hiring and discrimination, pay gaps, elites, and how organizations and labor markets reproduce or reduce inequality; also inequality by race, ethnicity, gender, and immigrant status, income and wage inequality, occupational segregation, and diversity in organizations.
